name: PT2399
description: The PT2399 is a single-chip CMOS echo/delay audio processor from Princeton Technology. It digitizes the input with an internal ADC, stores samples in 44Kbit of on-chip RAM, and reconstructs the delayed signal through an internal DAC, giving low noise (No about -90dBV) and low distortion (THD < 0.5%). Delay time is set by the clock frequency, which is controlled by an external resistor on the VCO pin (pin 6); larger resistance gives longer delay but rising distortion. The chip also provides two on-board op-amps and two low-pass filter stages used to build the analog input, feedback, and reconstruction filtering around the delay core. It runs from a single 5V supply and is the workhorse of countless DIY guitar delay/echo pedals and karaoke mixers.

extra.architecture: internal ADC + DAC, digital delay, internal VCO clock
extra.delay_range: approx 30ms to 340ms set by external R on VCO pin

typical_application: Analog guitar/vocal echo and delay effect where an external resistor on pin 6 sets the delay time and the internal op-amps build the feedback (repeats) path.
gotchas: Delay time is set by the resistor on VCO (pin 6); longer delays (higher R) sharply increase noise and distortion, so the usable musical range is roughly 30 to 340ms.
Has separate AGND (pin 3) and DGND (pin 4); keep their grounding clean to minimize clock noise bleeding into audio.
There is no internal feedback for repeats; the echo repeat/regeneration loop must be built externally using the on-chip op-amps.
It is a sampled (digital) delay, not a bucket-brigade BBD device, despite its analog-friendly application circuit.
Pin 1 is the only supply (VCC); REF on pin 2 is a half-supply bias node, not a second power input.
